# Ferdinand Lauren — The Systems Workbench

Computer Science undergraduate at Universitas Lampung (2022 cohort), based in Bandar Lampung,
Indonesia. Building towards IT business analysis and ERP functional consulting.

Positioning: entry-level. No industry experience claimed.

Working sequence: observe → define → design → verify. It is a personal working approach,
practised on one independent concept project and on coursework — not a methodology validated in
client engagements.

## What this site contains

- One in-depth case study, GYM-QR: a self-initiated gym attendance and locker management concept.
  It is documented as a concept, not client work. Includes a 1,166-line PRD, two state machines,
  15 acceptance scenarios, and 130 passing automated tests in the source repository.
- The Decision Lab: four documented decision cases from that system, with the initial conditions,
  the rules, the response, the resulting state, edge cases, and the evidence level for each.
- The AI Workbench: AI positioned as a drafting tool inside a reviewed workflow. It claims no
  time saving, no productivity metric, and no specific requirement written by a model.
- Coursework: Prak_WebLanjut, wuish, UAS-DSP, DSP, BMI_Calculator, pastebin. Labelled as coursework.

## Pages

- / — the desk, working approach, featured case file, Decision Lab, AI Workbench, selected work,
  about and contact
- /work/gym-qr — the case study as a document: observe, analyse, define, verify, reflect
